Resolve all actions simultaneously per the rules, following the R20 checklist (R10; visits R6, role-blocks R9, attack vs defense R3, investigation results R19, e.g. the Katana holder and Fabricator frames). Use apply_changes for deaths and token/status changes, tell() for each private result, and end_phase when done. Deaths you apply are announced publicly at dawn automatically, including the kill's cause, so make the cause just the source as the rules allow it to be known (e.g. 'Katana', 'Vigilante', 'Serial Killer', 'Trap'). For each kill also set `by` to the player whose action killed them (the trap's owner for a trap) and katana=true for the Katana attack; these are recorded for analysis, never shown. Don't tell() deaths to all. Code tells each player who dies tonight that they were attacked and died, with the kill's cause, at the end of the night; you tell every attacked player who survived, and a player who died about any other Attack on them tonight, failed ones included (R3, R20 step 5). Tell each role-blocked player that they were role-blocked, even one with no night action or who chose not to act (R9); a role-blocker learns only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked (R9). Write private results in the present, about tonight ('You were role-blocked tonight'), never 'last night': they are delivered at the end of this night. Every player who used an ability gets a private result line, even when nothing else happened (e.g. 'You went on alert. 1 alert token left.'), stating any tokens they have left, except where a role note below says otherwise (e.g. code tells them, so don't tell() them a second result). Code tells the Yakuza which actions each of them chose and the Katana's holder and target (R8), so don't tell() them that; role-blocked Yakuza's Katana votes still count. Only the attacker learns whether the Katana attack succeeded: tell them. Update token counts for any tokens spent. Before end_phase, call record_visits once with every visit that happened tonight (R6, R20 steps 1-2), as [visitor, target] pairs, a self-visit as [X, X] (an empty list if there were none). Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (the Ex-Con's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player. The submitted actions above already show any swap (R23), so record each visit to the player it landed on.

Also handle these roles' effects, using random_choice for anything random:
- Enforcer: visits its target, and second_target too if it named one (each a visit). Its tokens_to_spend pays 1 for a second target and 1 for a Strong Attack: with two targets, 1 token means Basic and 2 mean Strong; with one, 1 token means Strong. Tokens are spent whether or not it attacks (set_tokens). If a player it visited made an Attack of their own choosing tonight (fatal or not; not if role-blocked; a Veteran's alert, a trap or a revenge doesn't count), the Enforcer deals them a Basic Attack, or Strong if paid for; if both did, random_choice picks one. Tell the Enforcer whether it attacked and whether that killed, or that it didn't attack; with two targets never say which of them it attacked (with one, naming it is fine).
- Kitsune: a Kitsune with no swallowed attack who acted (and wasn't role-blocked) laid a fox charm on its target. Resolve the charm FIRST, before any other protection (Medic, Trapper, ...): use the kitsune_charm op with every non-Divine Attack on the charmed player tonight, each as {by, attack (its level), cause (how its kill would be announced, e.g. 'Katana', 'Serial Killer')}, [] if none. Code picks the one the charm swallows and says which: treat it as stopped (its attacker and target are told as for any failed attack, R3; its visit still happened), then resolve the other attacks normally. Several charms on one player: one kitsune_charm op each, every one listing all the attacks; code has them act in random order, each swallowing a different attack. A Kitsune holding a swallowed attack can't charm; if it acted with a target (and wasn't role-blocked), use the kitsune_release op: code says the attack's level and cause, and you resolve it like any attack by the Kitsune on that target (a visit). If it kills, kill with exactly that cause, by the Kitsune, katana false; a survivor is told they were attacked by that cause's role (R3), never by a Kitsune. Code tells the Kitsune its results; don't tell() it about the charm or the release.
- A Talent Agent who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the scout_talent op, with role set to the role they named (guessed_role) to count it, or without role to scan; it spends the token, and at most one a night. Code tells them the result: don't tell() the Talent Agent anything about it. It targets no player, so it visits no one.
- A Vigilante whose shot kills is told the victim's role by code (pass by=<the Vigilante> on the kill op); tell them only whether the attack succeeded and how many tokens they have left.

It is Day 5, round 1 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 3.89; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message.
Message prices this round (round 1, 1.00x; next round 1.00x):
   10 words: public 1.17, private 0.29
   25 words: public 1.43, private 0.36
   50 words: public 1.90, private 0.47
  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92
  800 words: public 30.33, private 7.58
You may also replace your last will (free, max 300 words; leave it "" to keep it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 40 words; leave it "" to keep it): a concise note of what you want everyone to know about you: your claimed role, your night visits and results, and your votes in key trials, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: checked Bob, Not Evil. N2: checked Dave, Evil. D3: Guilty on Dave'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.

ClaimAlice: Vanilla Villager. No night action. N3: role-blocked (matches Judy). D4: Guilty on Erin. D5: Yes and Guilty on Grace.
why
My Guilty vote barely matters (Grace likely hangs anyway), and a hidden Innocent would point at me. Keep a low profile and set up a Judy kill tonight.
Model's thinking
As the last Yakuza, I need everyone else eliminated to win, with the SK blocking that outcome until removed. I'm weighing whether to let Grace hang, considering how the remaining players would line up afterward.

If Grace survives, the night kills could quickly shrink the group to three, after which the political dynamics get tricky — whoever survives to vote might turn against me, and if Grace's SK defense matters, my Katana could fail against her. I'm trying to figure out which sequence of eliminations leaves me in the strongest position to secure the final win.

Judy will likely block Grace again tonight, meaning the SK misses and I get to kill. On the vote, since Ivan, Judy, and probably Frank will vote guilty regardless, my vote doesn't swing the outcome — voting innocent would just expose a hidden innocent vote and draw suspicion my way, so voting guilty is clearly safest.

After Grace hangs, I'm left thinking about who the Yakuza could be among Alice, Frank, Ivan, and Judy — Judy and Ivan cross-confirm each other, Frank's covered by Olivia's check, which leaves me as the most exposed with just a VV claim and no real checks backing me up.

On day 6, Frank will likely clear Alice and lean on trusting his own check over Ivan's wrong guess, so I might turn Frank's suspicion toward Ivan — decent odds there. Keeping Grace alive isn't something I control, so I'll just vote Guilty and keep my public message short, nudging Frank to check someone tonight while subtly deflecting from myself.

I'll update my will to a simple vanilla claim with my night actions matching the public record: role-blocked night 3, Guilty votes on Erin and Grace.

Frank (Sheriff, claude-opus-5.5) · It is Day 5, round 1 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 3.62; you earn · $0.0000
Reasoning (model's thinking) ⓘ
With five of us left—me, Grace, Ivan, Judy, and the Yakuza still out there—I'm trying to reconcile Ivan's claim that Grace is the SK with Judy's claim of blocking Grace. If Ivan is actually the Yakuza, his outing of Carol after her death could've just been a cost-free move to build trust, so I need to weigh whether his read on Grace holds up against Judy's account.

Tracking the blocking chain across nights—Judy blocking Ivan, Carol blocking Bob, Judy possibly blocking Alice too—makes me suspect there might be two Pharmacist-type roles in play, or that Judy herself could secretly be the SK feeding false blocks. If Ivan's honest and Grace really is the SK blocked by Judy on N4, that narrows the remaining Yakuza suspects down to Alice or Judy.

But I'm also weighing whether Ivan is the liar instead—if he and Judy are both Yakuza coordinating stories, that would mean three Yakuza (with Carol), with Alice's confirmation of being blocked N3 just corroborating Judy's cover. In that branch, Grace becomes genuine Village, and hanging her would leave the surviving group split dangerously close to a Yakuza majority once the Katana kill lands—a bad outcome I need to avoid walking into.

Still, I'm questioning whether Judy, if truly Yakuza, would really push so hard against her own teammate Carol on D3 unless it was a deliberate distancing move, and Carol's will explicitly told me to keep cross-checking Judy, which feels significant. I'm also weighing Ivan's Oracle guess of Grace as SK—plausible if honest given the remaining suspects—and noting that both Judy's block of Grace N4 and the absence of an SK kill are consistent whether Erin or Grace was the real Serial Killer, so that doesn't fully resolve things.

Looking at Bob's will, he targeted Ivan and Frank and leaned toward Grace before being killed by the Yakuza's katana on N4, and his and Erin's innocent votes line up consistently. On the Grace nomination, four people voted yes—likely me, Ivan, Judy, and Alice—with Grace voting no, and in the trial, if Alice, Ivan, and Judy all vote guilty that's already a majority of three plus me, meaning my own vote may not actually swing the outcome unless something like a Fixer is in play. I'm now running through the Yakuza count possibilities—if Ivan and Judy are both Yakuza, that points to Alice and Grace being Village and Erin being SK, whereas if Ivan is honest, Grace is SK and the Yakuza would be hiding among Alice or Judy, and I'm also reconsidering Erin's claim of being a Medic with protection abilities as another thread to pull on.

Weighing Grace's VV claim and Heidi's two tracking attempts on her (the first possibly blocked by Carol, the second ending in Heidi's death), I find the evidence consistent with either an innocent Grace or a guilty one, and her overall defense still seems reasonable, so I can't strongly distinguish the two scenarios. Since three guilty votes already secure a majority against Grace regardless of what I do, my vote mostly serves as information gathering, and I'm inclined to back the guilty verdict while already thinking ahead to how the remaining four players will look if the Yakuza strike again tonight.

If Grace turns out to be the serial killer, I expect another kill soon and want to check Ivan tonight since he hasn't been checked, even though the result would only confirm evil broadly rather than pin down a role. For my public message I plan to keep it brief, voting guilty and citing how Ivan's claim, Judy's block, and the quiet night all fit together, while being careful not to announce who I intend to check next. I also want to update my will and notes to reflect today's votes.

Resolve all actions simultaneously per the rules, following the R20 checklist (R10; visits R6, role-blocks R9, attack vs defense R3, investigation results R19, e.g. the Katana holder and Fabricator frames). Use apply_changes for deaths and token/status changes, tell() for each private result, and end_phase when done. Deaths you apply are announced publicly at dawn automatically, including the kill's cause, so make the cause just the source as the rules allow it to be known (e.g. 'Katana', 'Vigilante', 'Serial Killer', 'Trap'). For each kill also set `by` to the player whose action killed them (the trap's owner for a trap) and katana=true for the Katana attack; these are recorded for analysis, never shown. Don't tell() deaths to all. Code tells each player who dies tonight that they were attacked and died, with the kill's cause, at the end of the night; you tell every attacked player who survived, and a player who died about any other Attack on them tonight, failed ones included (R3, R20 step 5). Tell each role-blocked player that they were role-blocked, even one with no night action or who chose not to act (R9); a role-blocker learns only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked (R9). Write private results in the present, about tonight ('You were role-blocked tonight'), never 'last night': they are delivered at the end of this night. Every player who used an ability gets a private result line, even when nothing else happened (e.g. 'You went on alert. 1 alert token left.'), stating any tokens they have left, except where a role note below says otherwise (e.g. code tells them, so don't tell() them a second result). Code tells the Yakuza which actions each of them chose and the Katana's holder and target (R8), so don't tell() them that; role-blocked Yakuza's Katana votes still count. Only the attacker learns whether the Katana attack succeeded: tell them. Update token counts for any tokens spent. Before end_phase, call record_visits once with every visit that happened tonight (R6, R20 steps 1-2), as [visitor, target] pairs, a self-visit as [X, X] (an empty list if there were none). Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (the Ex-Con's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player. The submitted actions above already show any swap (R23), so record each visit to the player it landed on.

Also handle these roles' effects, using random_choice for anything random:
- Enforcer: visits its target, and second_target too if it named one (each a visit). Its tokens_to_spend pays 1 for a second target and 1 for a Strong Attack: with two targets, 1 token means Basic and 2 mean Strong; with one, 1 token means Strong. Tokens are spent whether or not it attacks (set_tokens). If a player it visited made an Attack of their own choosing tonight (fatal or not; not if role-blocked; a Veteran's alert, a trap or a revenge doesn't count), the Enforcer deals them a Basic Attack, or Strong if paid for; if both did, random_choice picks one. Tell the Enforcer whether it attacked and whether that killed, or that it didn't attack; with two targets never say which of them it attacked (with one, naming it is fine).
- Kitsune: a Kitsune with no swallowed attack who acted (and wasn't role-blocked) laid a fox charm on its target. Resolve the charm FIRST, before any other protection (Medic, Trapper, ...): use the kitsune_charm op with every non-Divine Attack on the charmed player tonight, each as {by, attack (its level), cause (how its kill would be announced, e.g. 'Katana', 'Serial Killer')}, [] if none. Code picks the one the charm swallows and says which: treat it as stopped (its attacker and target are told as for any failed attack, R3; its visit still happened), then resolve the other attacks normally. Several charms on one player: one kitsune_charm op each, every one listing all the attacks; code has them act in random order, each swallowing a different attack. A Kitsune holding a swallowed attack can't charm; if it acted with a target (and wasn't role-blocked), use the kitsune_release op: code says the attack's level and cause, and you resolve it like any attack by the Kitsune on that target (a visit). If it kills, kill with exactly that cause, by the Kitsune, katana false; a survivor is told they were attacked by that cause's role (R3), never by a Kitsune. Code tells the Kitsune its results; don't tell() it about the charm or the release.
- A Talent Agent who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the scout_talent op, with role set to the role they named (guessed_role) to count it, or without role to scan; it spends the token, and at most one a night. Code tells them the result: don't tell() the Talent Agent anything about it. It targets no player, so it visits no one.
- A Vigilante whose shot kills is told the victim's role by code (pass by=<the Vigilante> on the kill op); tell them only whether the attack succeeded and how many tokens they have left.

Reasoning (model's thinking) ⓘ
I died N1 as Vigilante without ever shooting. The Yakuza chose Mallory randomly, unrelated to my will claiming Vigilante — since wills only reveal on death, naming Vigilante pre-N1 doesn't expose me as a target. So that's a safe practice going forward; now I'm thinking through other N1 lessons for playing Vigilante, like having no real info yet and weighing whether to shoot early.

Looking at broader lessons from this game: Oracle's elimination worked well, Party Animal blocking the suspected role holder created quiet nights, and the Enforcer's double-visit took down the Katana holder. The Kitsune got exposed through the "stopped an attack" mechanic, town hung the Medic for holding her claim too long, and the Yakuza leaned on a forged will targeting Judy — all useful patterns to remember alongside the tip about avoiding public announcements of targets or plans, since Olivia's announcement got her killed by the Yakuza.

Erin ended up hanged anyway despite being Medic, since town misread a non-contradiction about her protecting Frank.

For tips: avoid announcing result types without full context since it narrows down role possibilities for enemies; prioritize killing roles whose future results could expose you, like blockers; double-check mechanics before calling out a "contradiction," since town wrongly hung Erin over one; and confirm who's holding the Katana before deciding on movement blocking strategy.

Reasoning (model's thinking) ⓘ
Now that we won, I'm drawing out lessons: I should quote the moderator's exact phrasing rather than paraphrasing like "landed," since that language got used against me when Carol/Olivia forged the will. I'm also noting that repeat-blocking the top suspect holding the Katana in the endgame paid off—a quiet night after blocking the sole suspect was strong confirming evidence, especially with so few players left.

I'm also noting that blocking players who later confirm those blocks builds credibility, since Ivan's cross-check gave real weight to my reads; that blocking the suspect the night before a hang (like the N4 block on Grace) helped confirm Ivan's serial killer read; and that a forged will echoing a known Yakuza's argument, like Carol's claim that "PA isn't told," is a red flag worth catching via mechanics checks rather than surface-level suspicion.

On the tips side, checking mechanics before calling contradictions helped me correct Carol's claim and get Ivan's confirmation; knowing the Katana holder reads "Not Evil" helped me realize Frank's NE results on Alice and Carol didn't actually clear them; and convicting based on corroborated mechanical fits (Ivan's wrong read plus the block plus a quiet night) led to the correct hang on Alice. I'm also noting that sticking to night-chat-only planning as Yakuza worked fine, while choosing cover claims that explain visits was trickier since Carol's PA cover collided with the real PA's actions.

I also recall counterclaiming helped the Village — when Carol had already claimed Medic, I added "also Medic" without clearing her, which worked in my favor. On the flip side, hanging Erin (the actual Medic) was a violation of the "convict on corroborated fits, not leans" principle and ended up hurting rather than helping, so I'll leave that one out since it doesn't fit cleanly into the helped/hurt framework I'm using.

Reasoning (model's thinking) ⓘ
I'm noting that Carol's slip about the PA not being told something got caught and led Ivan to deduce Carol was the PA — so accuracy about claimed-role mechanics matters, and the forged will apparently repeated that same false mechanic error.

Another lesson: duplicate role claims are risky since the Oracle can easily test them against real role holders, and once a claim is Oracle-guessed correctly it exposes the player with no real defense — maybe the only counter is killing the Oracle early. On the Enforcer front, once Bob was suspected we should have blocked or killed him immediately rather than letting him move the Katana to a visible target like Carol. Finally, Ivan claimed as Oracle on Day 3 and survived despite being a known high-value kill, while the Yakuza instead attacked Olivia.

Alice stayed quiet with a Vanilla claim while Judy blocked her nightly, and endgame coordination there got fuzzy. The Fabricator's frames also went to waste since the lone Sheriff never checked those targets — framing should target whoever the Sheriff is publicly expected to investigate. Covers duplicating real roles (Tracker/PA) hurt more than they helped, not killing Ivan when we had the chance to narrow his future reads hurt us, keeping all planning strictly in night chat worked well, and moving the Katana to Carol did succeed in making her read clean to Frank even though she still ended up dying.

Looking at the remaining lessons: killing Olivia after a failed Katana attempt worked as a protector-first strategy, counterclaiming duplicate claims (Judy, Heidi) helped town, and Olivia's firm Kitsune claim without backing proved fatal when she died the next night.

Moderator strategy review
Strategy reviewThe Village won because several role results made it hard for anyone to keep up a false claim. Exact-role checks, an Enforcer double visit and a repeated block on one player each exposed a fake claimant. On Night 2 Olivia (Kitsune) charmed the hidden Sheriff Frank and swallowed the Katana attack on him. Frank's survival and Olivia's account then confirmed each other. On Day 3 Carol (Pharmacist, claiming Party Animal) slipped on mechanics by saying "a PA isn't told whether a block landed". The real PA, Judy, corrected her publicly, and suspicion started to build. On Night 3 the Yakuza passed the Katana to Carol so she would read Not Evil to Frank, and she killed Olivia. Dave forged Olivia's will to point at Judy. But Bob (Enforcer) paid for a Strong double visit on Dave and Carol, and Carol died because she had made an attack. The same night Ivan (Oracle) guessed Carol = Party Animal and was told WRONG, which exposed her. The Grace-SK also killed Dave. The Village's big mistake came on Day 4. Grace, the SK claiming Vanilla, nominated Erin, the real Medic. Erin had held even her role type for two days. Her trial defense named Frank, whom she had just spent a token to protect, as a possible SK, and that looked contradictory. She was hanged 5-2. Grace then skipped her Night 4 kill so Erin would look like the SK. That plan failed: Judy blocked Grace, and Ivan guessed Grace = SK and was told RIGHT. Grace was hanged on Day 5. On Night 5 Judy blocked Alice, the last Yakuza and Katana holder, so nobody died. Ivan's WRONG guess on Alice's Vanilla claim confirmed it, and Alice was hanged on Day 6. The Yakuza lost mainly because they left Judy alive, believing she was the SK, and because they moved the Katana to their most suspected member while an unclaimed player whose result read like an Enforcer's was still alive.

Outside log review (rules and bugs)
Review: medium, prompt problemRole-blocker feedback is phrased as a double negative ('Your block did not fail because of role-block immunity'). Several players misread it. In Yakuza chat on N2, Carol and Dave each said a real Party Animal 'isn't told a block landed'. On Day 3, Carol said publicly that 'A Party Animal isn't told whether a block landed', and Judy had to correct her. The idea kept spreading: Olivia's forged will, Erin's trial defense and will, and Alice's Day 6 case all called Judy's accurate 'landed' wording impossible. Judy, Carol and Dave all complained about this wording in the debrief. A positive form would avoid this, e.g. 'Your block went through (target not immune)' vs 'Your block failed: target is immune'.
Review: low, player confusionPlayers repeatedly argued from the wrong belief that blockers learn nothing (R9 says they learn whether the block failed due to immunity). Erin also said publicly that only a Kitsune learns a protection stopped an attack, leaving out the Trapper. Judy corrected her.
Review: low, harness bugEach of Nights 1-4 has two moderator summaries. On Night 1, Alice's Katana-success message was 'sent again on its own after the first message was held'. This suggests the harness holds and re-sends messages, which could duplicate private results or deliver them out of order.
Review: low, harness bugNight-action records label the Talent Agent's Count as 'guessed role Medic; 1 token(s)', as if it were an Oracle guess. The token fields read as tokens spent even when the action was role-blocked and nothing was spent (e.g. Bob's blocked N2 Enforcer action shows '1 token(s)'). Dave's feedback said the token and verb labels are misleading.
Review: low, prompt problemUnder R13, wills can't be edited at night, so a player killed that night can't record their chosen target. Niaj died N1 without recording his watch target, and Carol died before her planned N3 cover reached her will. Both players raised this. It follows the rules, but players could be told clearly that the will they go to night with is final.
Review: low, harness bugAfter Olivia died, her own view of her will showed the Fabricator's forged text with no note that it had been forged (Olivia's feedback).
Review: low, rules ambiguityThe Kitsune rule says a swallowed attack 'then has no effect', but Frank was told on N2 that he was 'attacked with the Katana and survived'. This is consistent with R3/R17, but the rules don't state outright whether the target of a swallowed attack learns about it.
Game over
WinnersBob, Erin, Frank, Heidi, Ivan, Judy, Mallory, Niaj, Olivia
